subject: research/selfrep-closure
professional: a referee for a manufacturing-systems / self-replicating-systems venue (closure engineering in the Freitas and Gilbreath NASA 1980/82 and Freitas & Merkle 2004 sense, RepRap literature); first checks: is the BOM faithful to the source, do the closure ratios recompute, does the line/part-count figure agree with RepRap's own published self-manufacturing share, are mass and cost inputs sourced, does the uncertainty analysis cover the errors that matter, and is anything new beyond counting one BOM

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 experiments/run.py` (0.6 s): results.txt byte-identical to the committed copy; `python3 experiments/figure.py`: SVG byte-identical. Independent script /tmp/claude-0/sc/recompute.py (no import of the package; own closure loop, own sensitivity with seed 12345, 4000 draws, base-2 log-uniform factors) reproduces every line/unit/mass/cost figure for both variants and all three shops (35.3/9.4/17.3/11.4; 43.1/42.1/22.4/15.9; brass+casting 45.1/44.2/24.1/21.1) and the 5-95% brackets within 1 point (printer cost [8.7-14.9] vs [9-15]; brass casting cost [16.1-27.4] vs [16-27]). External anchors: with the 13 fastener lines excluded the printer makes 18/38 = 47.4% of lines, consistent with the ~48% of parts excluding fasteners the RepRap project quotes for Darwin/Mendel (Wikipedia 'RepRap'); assumed steel-rod masses agree with geometry x 7.85 g/cm3 (ISO 898-1 M8 stress area 36.6 mm2; 8 mm smooth rod) within 7% on all 7 rod lines. The BOM itself could not be checked against the wiki (reprap.org and web.archive.org refused by the proxy). Arithmetic is right given its inputs; held at 3 because the inputs that set mass and cost closure are assumed.
evidence.completeness: README deliverables: 51-line BOM with two bearing variants (present, bom.py), three seed shops (present), closure by lines/units/mass/cost (works), sensitivity bracket (works), vitamin and feedstock lists (in results.txt), figure (regenerates identically), reproduce commands (work, standard library only). No stubs/TODOs. Against the PROJECTS.md:189 milestone spec, 'a graph of parts, materials and processes' is a flat list and 'a source for each figure' is unmet for masses and costs (disclosed as an owner step). Live page could not be loaded (proxy 403 on marisstella.app).
evidence.verification: `cd research/selfrep-closure && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: Ran 8 tests, OK, 0.02 s. No test pinned any headline number. Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: caught 1 (brass bushing needs cast+cnc -> cast only); survived 4: units counted as 1 per line (closure.py:28), printed-part cost 0.5 -> 5.0 (bom.py:33, moves every cost figure), MDF plate made by the printer (bom.py:65, moves the printer-alone headline), cost percentiles replaced by constants (closure.py:48). test_figure only checks the SVG against the committed results.txt, never that results.txt matches the code.
evidence.craft: Read src/selfrep_closure/bom.py (74 lines), closure.py (56), experiments/run.py, figure.py, tests/test_closure.py, test_figure.py. Small, stdlib, seeded, data and reasons together in Part.why. Defects: makers tuple means 'any one suffices', so the one part needing two processes is special-cased by name prefix in makeable (closure.py:14-15); dense one-line multi-statement style; mass/cost default via `mass or {...}` treats an empty dict as absent; quantile by index truncation; `import math` inside a function.
evidence.claims: Checked the README table, bullets, research/README.md bullet and projects.json summary against results.txt: every percentage backed. Disclosures are strong (masses/costs assumed, process assignments judgement, fastener box sizes, one product only). Gaps: 'Mass and cost closure stay below 25% and 21%' while brass+casting cost is 21.1%; README '6 tests' (8 ran); the robustness claim 'across the sensitivity range at most 30%' rests on an independent-per-line scaling that averages errors away: scaling all printed-part costs jointly by 2 moves printer-alone cost closure from 11.4% to 34.1% (recompute.py), so the bracket understates the uncertainty a reader takes from it.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: RepRap's own self-manufacturing share (Jones et al., Robotica 2011; Sells, Bath PhD thesis 'Towards a self-manufacturing rapid prototyping machine', 2009: ~48% of Darwin parts excl. fasteners, 94% target), closure engineering (Freitas & Gilbreath, NASA CP-2255, 1982; Freitas & Merkle 2004 KSRM), cyclic fabrication systems (Moses, Yamaguchi & Chirikjian 2014), Ellery (2016) on closure for lunar self-replication. The result (one BOM counted by process) is a correct, reusable bookkeeping baseline that about 20 later selfrep-* projects build on, but it is not new, does not report the comparison with RepRap's own figure, and is not a PhD-level programme (absent from research/PROGRAMMES.md). A researcher can reuse the BOM; the assumed inputs propagate downstream.
evidence.domain: Against closure-engineering practice (closure by parts, mass, energy and information, Freitas & Gilbreath 1982): parts and mass closure are computed; energy and information closure are absent; cost closure counts the value of imported feedstock (filament, aluminium) inside makeable parts as closed, so it is not a value-added closure; masses that are derivable (rods from geometry, NEMA17 from datasheets ~280-350 g, printed parts from STL volumes) are left as placeholders; process assignments (router-cut GT2 pulleys, router-cut aluminium washers replacing steel ones) are optimistic and disclosed; the uncertainty analysis ignores correlated error. A referee would accept the counting and ask for sourced inputs and a correlated sensitivity.

No test pins any headline closure value; 4 of 5 seeded mutants (unit counting, printed-part cost, MDF makers, cost percentiles) survive

Masses and costs left as placeholders though derivable (rod masses match geometry x density within 7%, motor datasheets, printed-part STL volumes, dated quotes); the PROJECTS.md milestone asked for a source for each figure
README does not compare with RepRap's own published self-manufacturing share (~48% of parts excl. fasteners); the model gives 47% on that basis, an unused consistency check

Closure-engineering prior work (Freitas & Gilbreath 1982 parts/mass/energy/information closure; Moses, Yamaguchi & Chirikjian 2014; Ellery 2016) not engaged; result is bookkeeping of one BOM, not novel and not a programme
'Mass and cost closure stay below 25% and 21%' while brass+casting cost closure is 21.1%
makers tuple means 'any one suffices', so the one two-process part is special-cased by name prefix in makeable(); milestone asked for a parts/materials/processes graph, implemented as a flat list
Cost closure counts the value of imported feedstock (filament, aluminium, MDF) inside makeable parts as closed, overstating value-added closure

verdict: Every reported closure figure recomputes exactly from an independent script and the experiments reproduce byte-for-byte, and on a fastener-free basis the model's 47% printer-alone line share agrees with RepRap's own ~48% figure. But the mass and cost columns rest on assumed inputs that could have been sourced, the sensitivity bracket assumes independent per-line errors and so understates the uncertainty (a correlated 2x on printed-part cost triples printer-alone cost closure, 11% -> 34%), the tests pinned no headline value (4 of 5 seeded mutants survived), and the work is a correct count of one known BOM rather than a new result. Does not meet the bar: verification 1, claims 2, median 2.
